hints: Start at the root and explore both children recursively.
Keep the node values on the current root-to-node path in a temporary list or string.
A node is a complete path endpoint only when both its left and right children are absent.
After finishing a child, backtrack so the next sibling uses the correct root-to-node path.
title: Binary Tree Paths Problem

notes: The root-to-leaf paths may be returned in any order.
For the platform's examples and hidden cases, paths are serialized as strings with `->` between consecutive node values.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 100].
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: There are two leaves: 5 on the left branch and 3 on the right branch, giving the two root-to-leaf paths.
The root is also a leaf because it has no children, so the only path contains the single node.

content.problemStatement:
With the `root` of a binary tree, output *all root-to-leaf paths in **any order***.

A **leaf** is a node with no children.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/03/12/paths-tree.jpg)

```
Input: root = [1,2,3,null,5]
Output: ["1->2->5","1->3"]
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: root = [1]
Output: ["1"]
```

**Constraints:**

* The number of nodes in the tree is in the range `[1, 100]`.
* `-100 <= Node.val <= 100`

notes: Outputs are compared as root-to-leaf path collections; because the problem permits any order, the judge should treat path-array ordering as irrelevant.
The implementation visits every node once. Path construction can copy up to O(h) characters/values per leaf, giving O(n*h) in the stated node-based analysis.
The output itself is not counted as auxiliary space.
solution.approach: Use depth-first search from the root. Maintain the current root-to-node path, append the node value when entering a node, and when a leaf is reached join the values with `->` and add the resulting string. Backtrack by removing the last value before returning to the parent.

optimal.complexity: O(n * h) time and O(h) auxiliary space, excluding output.
optimal.description: Perform one DFS while maintaining a mutable path buffer. Add a path only at a leaf, then backtrack before exploring the next branch. This avoids rebuilding the traversal state from the root for every leaf while preserving the required output.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n * h) time and O(h) auxiliary space, excluding output.
bruteForce.description: Enumerate every root-to-leaf path with a DFS and construct each path independently from the root. This is straightforward and correct, with the same asymptotic bound as the intended solution because every reported path must be materialized.

solution.timeComplexity: O(n * h), where n is the number of nodes and h is the tree height, because a path of length O(h) is materialized for each leaf.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(h) auxiliary space for the DFS path and recursion stack, excluding the returned output.

followUps: Can you implement the DFS iteratively with an explicit stack?
How would the auxiliary space change for a highly skewed tree?
Can you avoid recursion while preserving left-to-right traversal order?

hidden.label: Complete tree with extra right leaf
Perfect tree at maximum branching for 15 nodes

learningObjectives: Recognize root-to-leaf traversal as a DFS/backtracking pattern.
Represent a tree path as a sequence and serialize it into the required string format.
Identify leaf nodes correctly and restore traversal state after recursive calls.
